reading.body:
Oregon's 2026 legislative record contains two AI-specific bills, and neither passed: SB1546 on AI companions and HB4103 on artificial intelligence both lack a status.

The rest of the docket is general state business. Twelve of the fifteen tracked bills passed, covering financial administration, batteries, elections, affordable housing, data brokers, economic development, public safety, medical assistance, and a memorial resolution. Two failed, on semi-independent state agencies and compensation for journalism. The AI bills sit in the same unresolved column as those failures, which is the only signal the data offers about their fate.

For AI specifically, the substantive action in Oregon this cycle came from the executive rather than the legislature. A September 24 executive order established AI procurement safeguards for state government, and it is the one item in this dataset that is both AI-focused and in force. Procurement rules shape what vendors can sell to the state, which is a narrower lever than a statute governing AI companions or AI generally, but it is a lever that was actually pulled.

What this does not tell the reader is why the two bills stalled, whether they return, or how the executive order will be enforced. It also says nothing about data centers, electricity, or computing hardware in Oregon, so no claim about the state's role in AI infrastructure can be drawn from it. The dataset covers fifteen bills and one news item, and that is the whole of its scope.
